title: Local Pdf generation
body:
As i am looking for a good invoicing app (previously used siwapp), i stumpled upon invoice ninja, which really looks awesome (only a little sad that it doesn't use symfony, which is my favorite framework :smile: but as the two frameworks are quite connected, i hope it will be no problem to get started with laravel)) 

for me it feels a little bit awkward to use a cloud service as pdf generation instance. 

especially if i use the invoice system on local system only, which is not publicly available (what i prefer for an invoice system). 

as @hillelcoren wrote [here](https://github.com/invoiceninja/invoiceninja/issues/587#issuecomment-167955413):

> for this to work your app instance must be publicly available

this is not really logic, if i have a public system, i don't require to send the pdfs to my users, they can login and view and download them there but if my system is not publicly available, i **must** attach the pdfs or else they can't read the invoice.

from the security point of view, i really don't like to send sensible invoice data, which contains customer data, prices, vat ids, ... to a cloud service.  this is also the reason why i am looking for a self hosted invoicing system, like yours is.

i would really love to see an option that i can choose to use the cloud service or a locally installed phantomjs 
- https://www.npmjs.com/package/phantomjs-prebuilt
- http://phantomjs.org/download.html

or by using php to create the pdf (i would prefer security over exact visual appearance of the pdf file (browser pdf vs attached pdf))
- https://packagist.org/packages/mpdf/mpdf
- https://packagist.org/packages/nitmedia/wkhtml2pdf
- https://packagist.org/packages/spipu/html2pdf
author: Participant 1

Thanks for your feedback!

Using a cloud service just makes our app easier to setup and use. We send our invoice links through email which can also be thought of as an insecure cloud service. 

If you're interested here's a post which describes setting it up locally using PhatomJS.

https://www.invoiceninja.com/forums/topic/api-email_invoice/#post-576

comments.body:
Hey @JeramyNS 

Our current solution is designed to make it as easy as possible to use/setup, by using phantomjscloud.com as long as the app is publicly accessible the feature just works. 

We've had requests to also support generating the PDF locally, if you're able to add the feature as an option it'd be great.

comments.author: Participant 4
comments.body:
Hello.

Any news or progress on this? @JeramyNS do you need help?

I'm highly interested in this topic, because I can't really use a service like phantomjscloud here in Germany. The data protection laws are very strict and prohibit sending the data of clients to servers outside of the European Union.

comments.author: Participant 3
comments.body:
I'm no longer actively working on these sorts of things anymore, however it really wouldn't be that hard for someone to create a page which works similar to the editing invoice page. 
It would generate the PDF code by visiting said page and then POST the generated invoice back to Invoice Ninja to store it in the DB and then redirect to back to the generated PDF. 
It should be a fairly easy thing to build, it would only require about 3 additional functions and one new template file so hopefully someone else has the time to integrate this for you

comments.author: Participant 3
comments.body:
Also, I was wondering what German laws you where referring to, as that sort of law has the potential to effect this project as well as future projects of my own.
Is this a blanket protection law or specific to your industry?

comments.author: Participant 4
comments.body:
Thanks for you reply.

The law is called "Bundesdatenschutzgesetz" and the specific part of the law is in § 4b. It is common law and not specific to any industry. As far as I know it is also a version of a European Law (and therefore not only German is affected) from 2010, since the "Safe Habor" agreement was canceled.

comments.author: Participant 3
comments.body:
Just had a quick read of the laws but from the looks of it you should still be able to send data to other countries for processing as long as the information is sent securely and follow their guidelines.
See: http://us.practicallaw.com/3-502-4080
Please forgive me if I missed anything, I can only see out of one eye today so it is a little hard to read properly.

comments.author: Participant 4
comments.body:
Yes, you can store/process the data outside of the EU, but they need to follow the exact guidelines which is very, very complicated.
It would also impact the reputation of a German company if they will store such information in the US or other countries outside of the EU. After the NSA scandals, the Germans are even more protective about their data.

comments.author: Participant 6
comments.body:
The problem with this is that I can't guarantee that the customer received the PDF before it may have been changed. I can't force him to download the version 1.0 of the invoice.

As described in #1219 you **can** change an already sent invoice without the customer noticing or any mention in the history/activity stream, by changing the description of a product. I still don't understand why this issue was closed.
Since I don't know if there are other occasions where a change in the invoice isn't reflected in the history, this "workaround" is just not safe enough.

I will have to send the PDF manually every time to be on the safe side for now, I guess...

comments.author: Participant 6
comments.body:
For those of you interested in already being able to provide a local phantomjs binary in the docker image, just add this to the dockerfile before setting of the default ENV variables (copied from https://github.com/wernight/docker-phantomjs/blob/master/Dockerfile):

```
# Install runtime dependencies
RUN apt-get update \
 && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        ca-certificates \
        bzip2 \
        libfontconfig 

RUN set -x  \
    # Install official PhantomJS release
 && apt-get update \
 && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        curl \
 && mkdir /tmp/phantomjs \
 && curl -L https://bitbucket.org/ariya/phantomjs/downloads/phantomjs-2.1.1-linux-x86_64.tar.bz2 \
        | tar -xj --strip-components=1 -C /tmp/phantomjs \
 && mv /tmp/phantomjs/bin/phantomjs /usr/local/bin
```

scope: Current retrievable issue body and issue comments; not the original study's historical snapshot. Linked pages and attachments are not fetched.
